note: Anchored: Jesus answers a test with Deut 8:3, 'Man shall not live on bread alone' (Matt 4:4; Luke 4:4), and Deut 8:3 is set in the manna: 'in your hunger He gave you manna to eat'. Deut 8:2 calls the forty years in the wilderness a test; Mark 1:13 and Luke 4:2: 'for forty days ... tempted'. Shared: Israel tested in the wilderness forty years and fed with manna; Jesus tested in the wilderness forty days, hungry, refusing to make bread of stones. Fasting 'forty days and forty nights' is also Moses' at Horeb (Deut 9:9), on the link to the giving of the law. The order of the three tests is Matthew's (manna, Massah, the law); Luke gives the last two the other way round (Luke 4:5-12), and Mark names the forty days but no quotation.

note: Anchored: Jesus answers a test with Deut 6:16, 'Do not put the Lord your God to the test' (Matt 4:7; Luke 4:12). note: Anchored twice. The fast: 'fasting forty days and forty nights' (Matt 4:2) is Moses' fast when he 'went up on the mountain to receive the tablets' and stayed 'forty days and forty nights. I ate no bread' (Deut 9:9; Exod 34:28). The answer: 'Worship the Lord your God and serve Him only' (Matt 4:10; Luke 4:8) quotes Deut 6:13, said in Deuteronomy's second telling of the law at Moab, which begins by retelling the commandments (Deut 5:2-21); against the devil's 'fall down and worship me' (Matt 4:9) stands 'You shall not bow down to them or worship them' (Deut 5:9). Deut 6:13's Hebrew reads 'fear' the LORD; Matthew and Luke read 'worship'. Shared: Moses forty days and nights without bread, receiving the law; Jesus forty days and nights fasting, answering the devil from it.

note: Anchored six times: the Sermon takes up the law's words, each time introduced 'You have heard that it was said' (5:31 'It has also been said') and followed by 'But I tell you'. Four are quoted (5:21, 5:27, 5:38, and 5:43's 'Love your neighbor'); 5:31 summarises Deut 24:1 (Matthew 'must give', Deuteronomy 'may write'), and 5:33 gathers several laws on oaths and vows (Lev 19:12; Num 30:2; Deut 23:21) rather than quoting one. The words were given at Sinai (Exod 20:13-14; Exod 21:24; Leviticus, 'on Mount Sinai', Lev 27:34) or set before Israel at Moab (Deut 4:44-46; Numbers, 'on the plains of Moab', Num 36:13) -- Deuteronomy itself tells the two apart: the covenant 'in the land of Moab, in addition to the covenant He had made with them at Horeb' (Deut 29:1). 'Said to the ancients' (5:21): the Greek dative can also be read 'by the ancients'. 'Hate your enemy' (5:43) is not in the law's text; only 'Love your neighbor' is (Lev 19:18). Shared: the law Israel received, its words taken up one by one. That the mountain of Matt 5:1 recalls Sinai is correspondence only and is not claimed. Matthew alone has these sayings in this form; Luke's sermon (Luke 6:27-36) has 'Love your enemies' without the quotations.

note: Declared: Jesus names the earlier account himself. In Luke 4:24-27 he cites Elijah and the widow of Zarephath (v. 26) and Elisha and Naaman (v. 27) as examples. Luke 4:27 sums up the Naaman account: of the many lepers in Israel in Elisha's time, only Naaman the Syrian was cleansed. Luke's 'cleansed' and 2 Kings' 'clean' are not one quotation. The Elijah account has no event record yet. (Was re_enacts until the eight-reader review, 2026-10-03: no scene is repeated at Nazareth, and the slot map 'sent to one outside Israel' was not true of Elisha -- Naaman came to him, 2 Kgs 5:9.)
